D.t: Jeff Merkley leads by 24.2 in the forecast and wins 100% of simulations. The cushion is about 496,523 votes; a one point swing is about 10,276 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +15.6 and D +32.6. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Multnomah, a projected net 282,706 votes; Washington, a projected net 123,538 votes; Lane, a projected net 65,652 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Marion, D +6.8, 6.9% of the vote; Jackson, D +4.0, 5.4% of the vote; Yamhill, D +1.9, 2.5% of the vote; Polk, D +4.6, 2.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Jeff Merkley runs furthest behind in Douglas, Klamath, Umatilla. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 86% of voters, 58 to 38, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.30 points; Voters without a degree, 59% of voters, 56 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.94 points; Men, 42% of voters, 56 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 2.09 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Jeff Merkley: Immigration voters 26 to 70, Small counties 44 to 52, Midsize counties 47 to 49. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$6.8M cash against $50K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
